s: Sutrakritanga, Book II has title Sutrakritanga, Book II
Sutrakritanga, Book II has date -0199/-0100
Sutrakritanga, Book II has source class canonical
Nirgrantha monks and nuns praised Mahâvîra
q: The Nirgrantha monks and nuns worshipped and praised the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra

s: Mahâvîra explain it (with its meaning, reasons, and arguments)
q: I shall tell, declare, explain, expound, and demonstrate it with its meaning, reasons, and arguments.

s: lotus-pool contains much water and mud (very full and complete)
q: There is a lotus-pool containing much water and mud, very full and complete, answering to the idea (one has of a lotus-pool)

s: lotus-pool is full of white lotuses (delightful, conspicuous, magnificent, and splendid)
q: full of white lotuses, delightful, conspicuous, magnificent, and splendid.

s: white lotuses are the best of Nymphaeas (tall, brilliant, of fine colour, smell, taste, and touch)
q: there grew many white lotuses, the best of Nymphaeas, as we are told, in beautiful array, tall, brilliant, of fine colour, smell, taste, and touch, (&c., all down to) splendid.

s: one big white lotus is a white lotus (the best of Nymphaeas)
q: there grew one big white lotus, the best of Nymphaeas

s: one big white lotus grows in lotus-pool (in the very middle)
q: And in the very middle of this lotus-pool there grew one big white lotus

s: first man is a man (knowing, clever, well-informed, discerning, wise, not foolish)
q: I am a knowing, clever, well-informed, discerning, wise, not foolish man

s: first man knows the way
q: who keeps the way, knows the way, and is acquainted with the direction and bent of the way.

s: first man enters lotus-pool (to fetch one big white lotus)
q: Having said this the man entered the lotus-pool.

s: Book II contains First Lecture, Called the Lotus
q: Second Book. First Lecture, Called the Lotus.

s: first man is stuck in mud (in the middle of the lotus-pool)
q: but in the middle of the lotus-pool he stuck in the mud.

s: second man is a man (knowing, clever, well-informed, discerning, wise, not foolish)
q: However, I am a knowing, clever, (&c., all down to the end of the paragraph) he stuck in the mud.' This was the second man.

s: second man comes from Southern quarter
q: There came a man from the Southern quarter to the lotus-pool

s: second man judges first man (as not knowing and not clever)
q: This man is not knowing, not clever, (&c., see above, all down to) not acquainted with the direction and bent of the way.

s: second man is stuck in mud (in the middle of the lotus-pool)
q: This was the second man. (The same thing happened to a third and a fourth man

s: monk knows the way (knowing, clever, and acquainted with the direction and bent of the way)
q: knowing, clever, (&c., all down to) acquainted with the direction and bent of the way

s: monk does not enter lotus-pool (standing on its bank)
q: Having said this the monk did not enter the lotus-pool; but standing on the bank of it he raised his voice

s: monk raise his voice
q: but standing on the bank of it he raised his voice: 'Fly up, O white lotus, best of Nymphaeas!'

s: First Lecture, Called the Lotus is called the Lotus
q: We now come to the Lecture called 'the Lotus.'

s: world is represented by lotus-pool (in the simile)
q: meaning the world I spoke of the lotus-pool.

s: Karman is represented by water (in the simile)
q: Meaning Karman I spoke of the water.

s: pleasures and amusements are represented by mud (in the simile)
q: Meaning pleasures and amusements I spoke of the mud.

s: people in general are represented by white lotuses (in the simile)
q: Meaning people in general I spoke of those many white lotuses, the best of Nymphaeas.

s: king is represented by one big white lotus (in the simile)
q: Meaning the king I spoke of the one big white lotus, the best of Nymphaeas.

s: heretical teachers are represented by four men (in the simile)
q: Meaning heretical teachers I spoke of those four men.

s: Law is represented by monk (in the simile)
q: Meaning the Law I spoke of the monk.

s: Sudharman is a speaker
q: O long-lived (Gambûsvâmin)! I (Sudharman) have heard the following Discourse from the Venerable (Mahâvîra).

s: Nirvâna is represented by flying up (in the simile)
q: Meaning Nirvâna I spoke of (the lotus') flying up.

s: king is a man (strong and governing a kingdom)
q: And of these men one man is king, who is strong like the great Himavat, Malaya, Mandara, and Mahêndra mountains, (&c., all down to) who governs his kingdom in which all riots and mutinies have been suppressed.

s: king has assembly of Ugras and sons of Ugras
q: And this king had an assembly of Ugras and sons of Ugras, Bhôgas and sons of Bhôgas, Aikshvâkas and sons of Aikshvâkas, Gñâtris and sons of Gñâtris, Kauravas and sons of Kauravas, warriors and sons of warriors, Brâhmanas and sons of Brâhmanas, Likkhavis and sons of Likkhavis, commanders and sons of commanders, generals and sons of generals.

s: heretical teachers teach religion (to a man full of faith)
q: Being professors of some religion (they thought) 'We shall teach him our religion.'

s: soul is identical with body (according to the first doctrine)
q: Upwards from the soles of the feet, downwards from the tips of the hair on the head, within the skin's surface is (what is called) Soul, or what is the same, the Âtman.

s: Âtman is identical with soul (according to the first doctrine)
q: within the skin's surface is (what is called) Soul, or what is the same, the Âtman.

s: body determines duration of soul (according to the first doctrine)
q: It lasts as long as the body lasts, it does not outlast the destruction (of the body).

s: Nâstikas deny soul (as something different from the body)
q: Therefore there is and exists no (soul different from the body).

s: Nâstikas deny world beyond
q: This murderer says: 'Kill, dig, slay, burn, cook, cut or break to pieces, destroy! Life ends here; there is no world beyond.'

s: Sudharman heard discourse from Mahâvîra
q: I (Sudharman) have heard the following Discourse from the Venerable (Mahâvîra).

s: Nâstikas engage in pleasures and amusements (for their own enjoyment)
q: Thus undertaking various works they engage in various pleasures and amusements for their own enjoyment.

s: Nâstikas are given to pleasures and amusements (greedy, fettered, passionate, covetous, and slaves of love and hate)
q: Thus they are given to pleasures, amusements, and sensual lust; they are greedy, fettered, passionate, covetous, the slaves of love and hate

s: Nâstikas cannot free themselves (from the Circle of Births)
q: therefore they cannot free themselves (from the Circle of Births), nor free anybody else from it

s: second doctrine: everything consists of the five elements asserts everything consists of the five elements (down to a blade of grass)
q: Everything down to a blade of grass (consists of them).

s: five elements are eternal (without beginning and end)
q: they are without beginning and end; they always produce effects, are independent of a directing cause or everything else; they are eternal.

s: five elements include earth (the first element)
q: Earth is the first element, water the second, fire the third, wind the fourth, and air the fifth.

s: five elements include water (the second element)
q: Earth is the first element, water the second, fire the third, wind the fourth, and air the fifth.

s: five elements include fire (the third element)
q: Earth is the first element, water the second, fire the third, wind the fourth, and air the fifth.

s: five elements include wind (the fourth element)
q: Earth is the first element, water the second, fire the third, wind the fourth, and air the fifth.

s: five elements include air (the fifth element)
q: Earth is the first element, water the second, fire the third, wind the fourth, and air the fifth.

s: third doctrine: the Self is the cause of everything asserts the Self is the cause of everything (all things have the Self for their cause and object)
q: Here all things have the Self for their cause and their object, they are produced by the Self, they are manifested by the Self, they are intimately connected with the Self, they are bound up in the Self.

s: third doctrine: the Self is the cause of everything rejects twelve Aṅgas (as wrong and not true)
q: And the twelve Aṅgas, the Canon of the Ganins, which has been taught, produced, and declared by the Sramanas, the Nirgranthas, viz. the Âkârâṅga (all down to) the Drishtivâda, is wrong, not true, not a representation of the truth

s: twelve Aṅgas is a Canon of the Ganins (taught, produced, and declared by the Sramanas, the Nirgranthas)
q: And the twelve Aṅgas, the Canon of the Ganins, which has been taught, produced, and declared by the Sramanas, the Nirgranthas

s: twelve Aṅgas includes Âkârâṅga (among the twelve Aṅgas)
q: viz. the Âkârâṅga (all down to) the Drishtivâda

s: twelve Aṅgas includes Drishtivâda (among the twelve Aṅgas)
q: viz. the Âkârâṅga (all down to) the Drishtivâda

s: fourth doctrine: Fate is the cause of everything asserts Fate is the cause of everything (movable and immovable beings are actuated by Fate)
q: Movable or immovable beings in all the four quarters thus (i.e. by the will of Fate) cone to have a body, to undergo the vicissitudes of life, to lose their body, to arrive at some state of existence, to experience pleasure and pain.

s: Fate causes pleasure and pain (according to the fourth doctrine)
q: Movable or immovable beings in all the four quarters thus (i.e. by the will of Fate) cone to have a body, to undergo the vicissitudes of life, to lose their body, to arrive at some state of existence, to experience pleasure and pain.

s: fourth doctrine: Fate is the cause of everything denies action (one kind of man does not admit action)
q: One man admits action, another man does not admit action.

s: Mahâvîra is a Venerable Ascetic
q: The Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra addressed the crowd of Nirgrantha monks and nuns

s: Sramanas is addressed as long-lived
q: I have told you, O long-lived Sramanas, a simile; you must comprehend the meaning of it.

s: Nirgrantha monks and nuns worshipped Mahâvîra
q: The Nirgrantha monks and nuns worshipped and praised the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra

s: men is a people (found in the East, West, North, and South)
q: I say: here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (&c., as in § 13, all down to) ugly men.

s: mendicant's life is a life of renunciation
q: Whether they have kinsmen and property or not, they renounce them and lead a mendicant's life.

s: pleasures and amusements include sounds
q: I enjoy sounds, colours, smells, tastes, and feelings of touch.

s: pleasures and amusements include colours
q: I enjoy sounds, colours, smells, tastes, and feelings of touch.

s: pleasures and amusements include smells
q: I enjoy sounds, colours, smells, tastes, and feelings of touch.

s: pleasures and amusements include tastes
q: I enjoy sounds, colours, smells, tastes, and feelings of touch.

s: pleasures and amusements include feelings of touch
q: I enjoy sounds, colours, smells, tastes, and feelings of touch.

s: pleasures and amusements cannot help or save men (in this life)
q: Here, in this life, pleasures and amusements are not able to help or to save one.

s: relations include kinsmen
q: There are things more intimately connected with me, viz. my mother, father, brother, sister, wife, children, grandchildren, daughters-in-law, servants, friends, kinsmen, companions, and acquaintances.

s: Âryas is a men
q: I say: here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (&c., as in § 13, all down to) ugly men.

s: relations cannot help or save men (because one person cannot experience another's pains)
q: Here, indeed, the bonds of relationship are not able to help nor save one.

s: death is individual individual experience (each person dies individually)
q: Individually a man is born, individually he dies, individually he falls (from this state of existence), individually he rises (to another).

s: body includes hands (part and parcel of the individual)
q: There are things more intimately connected with me, viz. my hands, feet, arms, legs, head, belly, character, life, strength, colour, skin, complexion, ear, eye, nose, tongue, and touch; they are part and parcel of me.

s: householders are killers of living beings
q: Here, indeed, householders are killers (of beings) and acquirers of property

s: householders are acquirers of possessions
q: Here, indeed, householders are killers (of beings) and acquirers of property

s: Sramanas include killers of living beings (some Sramanas and Brâhmanas)
q: Here, indeed, householders are killers (of beings) and acquirers of property, and so are even some Sramanas and Brâhmanas.

s: Brâhmanas include acquirers of property (some Sramanas and Brâhmanas)
q: Here, indeed, householders are killers (of beings) and acquirers of property, and so are even some Sramanas and Brâhmanas.

s: monk is a non-killer of living beings
q: But I am no killer (of beings) nor an acquirer of property.

s: non-Âryas is a men
q: I say: here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (&c., as in § 13, all down to) ugly men.

s: monk leads chastity (relying upon non-killing and non-acquisition)
q: Relying upon householders and such Sramanas and Brâhmanas as are killers (of beings) and acquirers of property, we shall lead a life of chastity.

s: monk avoids love and hatred (as causes of sin)
q: But a monk who takes this into consideration, should lead a life subject to neither (love nor hatred).

s: Law prohibits violence (toward all living beings)
q: He should preach the Law which prohibits to kill any living being, after having well considered it.

s: living beings include earth-lives (one of the six classes)
q: The Venerable One has declared that the cause (of sins) are the six classes of living beings, earth-lives, &c.

s: living beings feel pain (when ill-treated)
q: in the same way, be sure of this, all kinds of living beings feel the same pain and agony, &c., as I, when they are ill-treated in the same way.

s: living beings should not be slain
q: all sorts of living beings should not be slain, nor treated with violence, nor abused, nor tormented, nor driven away.

s: monk abstains from sin (by controlling himself and ceasing to acquire gross Karman)
q: In this way a monk ceases to acquire gross Karman, controls himself, and abstains from sins.

s: monk does not acquire food (when bought, stolen, or forcibly taken for his sake)
q: A monk should not take food, drink, dainties, and spices when he knows that (the householder) to satisfy him, or for the sake of a co-religionist, has bought or stolen or taken it

s: food be sufficient for to practise control and to carry the burden of it (just sufficient)
q: it greases, as it were, the axle of the carriage and anoints the sore, being just sufficient to enable one to practise control and to carry the burden of it

s: monk preaches Law (for no other motive than the annihilation of Karman)
q: but he should preach the Law indefatigably, for no other motive than the annihilation of Karman.

s: men own houses (small or large)
q: They own small or large houses and fields, they own few or many servants and peasants.

s: Law leads to final beatitude (for those who exert themselves well)
q: Those heroes of faith who are instructed in the Law by such a monk and exert themselves well, are possessed of all (virtues), abstain from all (sins), cease from all (passions), conduct themselves well in every way, and reach final beatitude.

s: monk seeks Liberation
q: Such a monk searches the Law, knows the Law, and endeavours to gain Liberation

s: monk possesses Samitis
q: he is free from passions, possesses the Samitis, is wise, always exerts himself

s: monk is free from passions
q: he is free from passions, possesses the Samitis, is wise, always exerts himself

s: men own fields (small or large)
q: They own small or large houses and fields, they own few or many servants and peasants.

s: men own servants (few or many)
q: They own small or large houses and fields, they own few or many servants and peasants.

s: men own peasants (few or many)
q: They own small or large houses and fields, they own few or many servants and peasants.

s: men lead mendicant's life (after renouncing possessions)
q: Being born in such-like families, they renounce (their possessions) and lead a mendicant's life.

s: renunciation of activity is a rejection of possessions and relations (undertaken by those leading a mendicant's life)
q: Some leave their kinsmen and their property to lead a mendicant's life; others, who have no kinsmen nor property, lead a mendicant's life. Whether they have kinsmen and property or not, they renounce them and lead a mendicant's life.

s: Sudharman heard discourse from Mahâvîra (as reported by Sudharman)
q: O long-lived (Gambûsvâmin)! I (Sudharman) have heard the following Discourse from the Venerable (Mahâvîra).

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning for one's interest (when injury is done for oneself or one's associates)
q: Thereby the, bad Karman accrues to him. This is the first kind of committing sins, that prompted by a motive.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning without a personal interest (when beings are killed without personal motive)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the second kind of committing sins, that prompted by no personal interest.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning by slaying (in retaliation for perceived injury)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the third kind of committing sins, called slaying.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning by an error of sight (when a friend or innocent person is mistaken for an enemy)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the fifth kind of committing sins, viz. by an error of sight.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning by lying (for oneself or one's associates)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the sixth kind of committing sins, viz. by lying.

s: bad Karman accrues from taking what is not freely given (for oneself or one's associates)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the seventh kind of committing sins, viz. by taking what is not freely given.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning by a mere conceit (through mental wrath, pride, deceit, or greed)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the eighth kind of committing sins, viz. by a mere conceit.

s: Mahâvîra is a Venerable
q: I (Sudharman) have heard the following Discourse from the Venerable (Mahâvîra).

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning through pride (when one exalts oneself and despises another)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the ninth kind of committing sins, viz. through pride.

s: bad Karman accrues from bad treatment of one's friends (through severe punishment of household members)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the tenth kind of committing sins, consisting in bad treatment of one's friends.

s: deceitful man is not trusted by men (in this world and the next)
q: A deceitful man is generally not trusted in this world, a deceitful man is not trusted in the next world.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning through deceit (when deception is concealed and not expiated)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the eleventh kind of committing sins, viz. through deceit.

s: bad Karman accrues from sinning through greed (when sensual pleasures are desired and defended)
q: Thereby the bad Karman accrues to him. This is the twelfth kind of committing sins, viz. through greed.

s: religious life involves acquiring Karman (through subtle actions of a self-controlled monk)
q: We now treat of the thirteenth kind of acquiring Karman, that having reference to religious life.

s: religious life is practised by monks (with control of mind, speech, body, and senses)
q: A monk who controls himself for the benefit of his soul, who in walking carefully avoids to cause the death of any living creature, who uses gentle and righteous speech, who receives alms in a manner to avoid the forty-two faults, who is careful in receiving and keeping of things necessary for religious exercises, who performs the operations of nature (excrements, urine, saliva, corporal impurities and mucus) in an unfrequented place, who is careful with regard to mind, speech, and body, who guards his mind, speech, and body so as to protect his soul from passions, who guards his senses, who leads a chaste life regulated by the three Guptis, who carefully walks, stands, sits down, lies down, and speaks, who carefully takes up and lays down his cloth, alms-bowl, blanket, broom,--(even) such a monk performs various subtile actions called îryapathika (if it did but consist in moving an eyelash).

s: religious life acquires Karman (called îryapathika)
q: This Karman is acquired and comes in contact (with the soul) in the first moment, in the second moment it is experienced, in the third it is destroyed; thus it is acquired, comes in contact (with the soul), takes rise, and is destroyed.

s: religious life not be the road to those who are freed from all misery
q: This conduct is unworthy, impure, void (of virtues), not holy, not right, not eradicating sins; it is not the road to perfection, liberation, Nirvâna, final delivery, not the road of those who are freed from all misery; it is thoroughly untrue, and bad.

s: occult sciences are practised for food (by unworthy and mistaken men)
q: These and similar sciences are practised (by some men) for the sake of food, drink, clothes, a lodging, a bed, and various objects of pleasure.

s: occult sciences lead to Asuras (after practitioners die at their allotted time)
q: After having died at their allotted time, they will be born in some places inhabited by Asuras and evildoers.

s: occult sciences lead to deaf and dumb people (after release from places inhabited by Asuras and evildoers)
q: And when they are released therefrom, they will again be born deaf and dumb, or night-blind.

s: men practise occult sciences (when differing in intellect, will, character, opinions, taste, undertakings, and plans)
q: Some men differing in intellect, will, character, opinions, taste, undertakings, and plans, study various evil sciences;

s: men are born in hell (when cruel and proud and accompanied only by Karman)
q: When he leaves this body and is only accompanied by his Karman, he, without a will of his own, goes forth from womb to womb, from birth to birth, from death to death, from hell to hell.

s: men enjoys human life (while causing others to suffer and die)
q: while they make suffer or kill, or make suffer and kill (beings), and do various evil deeds, they enjoy the excellent pleasures of human life;

s: noble men judge men (who maintain themselves by cruel actions)
q: But noble men who see him will say: 'This man does cruel actions, and maintains himself by them. His is the southern region, the hell, the dark fortnight. In the future he will not easily obtain enlightenment.'

s: perfection is a goal of the religious path (together with liberation, Nirvâna, and final delivery)
q: it is not the road to perfection, liberation, Nirvâna, final delivery, not the road of those who are freed from all misery;

s: soul experience disturbance
q: The former is when the Self is) at rest, (the latter, when it is) in disturbance.

s: Liberation is a goal of the religious path (together with perfection, Nirvâna, and final delivery)
q: it is not the road to perfection, liberation, Nirvâna, final delivery, not the road of those who are freed from all misery;

s: Nirvâna is a goal of the religious path (together with perfection, liberation, and final delivery)
q: it is not the road to perfection, liberation, Nirvâna, final delivery, not the road of those who are freed from all misery;

s: final beatitude is a goal of the religious path (together with perfection, liberation, and Nirvâna)
q: it is not the road to perfection, liberation, Nirvâna, final delivery, not the road of those who are freed from all misery;

s: demerit is a bad Karman
q: This is the explanation of the first subject, viz. demerit.

s: living beings feel pain (when committing sin)
q: And as regards committing of sin, among denizens of hell, brute animals, gods, men, and whatever other suchlike beings there be, the sentient beings feel the pain.

s: thirteen kinds of committing sins is a activities (practised by sentient beings)
q: And these beings practise the following thirteen kinds of activity-- 1. sinning for one's interest; 2. sinning without a personal interest; 3. sinning by slaying; 4. sinning through accident; 5. sinning by an error of sight; 6. sinning by lying; 7. sinning by taking what is not freely given; 8. sinning by a mere conceit; 9. sinning through pride; 10. sinning through bad treatment of one's friends; 11. sinning through deceit; 12. sinning through greed; 13. actions referring to a religious life.

s: thirteen kinds of committing sins number thirteen
q: And these beings practise the following thirteen kinds of activity-- 1. sinning for one's interest; 2. sinning without a personal interest; 3. sinning by slaying; 4. sinning through accident; 5. sinning by an error of sight; 6. sinning by lying; 7. sinning by taking what is not freely given; 8. sinning by a mere conceit; 9. sinning through pride; 10. sinning through bad treatment of one's friends; 11. sinning through deceit; 12. sinning through greed; 13. actions referring to a religious life.

s: merit is a subject of explanation (second subject)
q: Now the explanation of the second subject, viz. merit, is as follows:

s: men are located in North (among the four directions)
q: Here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (all down to) ugly men.

s: men are located in South (among the four directions)
q: Here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (all down to) ugly men.

s: men include Âryas
q: Here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (all down to) ugly men.

s: men include non-Âryas
q: Here in the East, West, North, and South there are some men, viz. Âryas, non-Âryas, (all down to) ugly men.

s: men own fields and houses (in the meritorious condition)
q: They own fields and houses, (&c., all as in II, 1, §§ 34-59, down to) reach final beatitude. (58)

s: householders are a men (in the demeritorious condition)
q: Here in the East, West, North, and South live some men; they are householders, men of great desires, great undertakings, great possessions, unrighteous men,

s: householders have great desires
q: they are householders, men of great desires, great undertakings, great possessions, unrighteous men,

s: householders have great undertakings
q: they are householders, men of great desires, great undertakings, great possessions, unrighteous men,

s: householders have great possessions
q: they are householders, men of great desires, great undertakings, great possessions, unrighteous men,

s: monks avoid death of any living creature (by walking carefully)
q: There are such monks as in walking carefully avoid to occasion the death of any living creature,

s: monks are regulated by Guptis (their chaste lives)
q: as lead chaste lives regulated by the three Guptis,

s: monks are free from Âsravas
q: as are calm, tranquil, passionless, happy, free from the Âsravas, and bondage, without sorrow;

s: monks are free from bondage
q: as are calm, tranquil, passionless, happy, free from the Âsravas, and bondage, without sorrow;

s: monks obtain Kêvala knowledge (at the end of their ascetic life)
q: they reach, while they are breathing their last, the highest knowledge and faith, called Kêvala, which is infinite, supreme, unobstructed, unimpeded, complete and full;

s: merit leads to final beatitude (through righteous conduct)
q: and then they obtain absolute perfection, enlightenment, deliverance, final beatitude, and put an end to all misery.

s: monks obtain perfection (after attaining Kêvala)
q: and then they obtain absolute perfection, enlightenment, deliverance, final beatitude, and put an end to all misery.

s: monks obtain enlightenment (after attaining Kêvala)
q: and then they obtain absolute perfection, enlightenment, deliverance, final beatitude, and put an end to all misery.

s: monks obtain deliverance (after attaining Kêvala)
q: and then they obtain absolute perfection, enlightenment, deliverance, final beatitude, and put an end to all misery.

s: followers of the Sramanas understand living beings (as distinct from things without life)
q: There are, for instance, followers of the Sramanas, who comprehend (the doctrine about) living beings and things without life,

s: followers of the Sramanas understand Âsravas (as part of their doctrine)
q: who are well grounded in (the knowledge of) the Âsravas, Samvara, the realisation and annihilation (of Karman), the subject of actions, bondage, and final liberation;

s: followers of the Sramanas understand Samvara (as part of their doctrine)
q: who are well grounded in (the knowledge of) the Âsravas, Samvara, the realisation and annihilation (of Karman), the subject of actions, bondage, and final liberation;

s: followers of the Sramanas support Nirgrantha Sramanas (by providing religious necessities)

Gradually increasing and attaining to the proper dimensions of a foetus they come forth from the womb, some as males, some as females, some as neuters.
